## Concrete remaining M1 contract

The contracts below preserve the canonical crate allowlist and source limits:
400 physical lines for production Rust, 600 for tooling/integration tests.
`wf-types`/`wf-domain` stay synchronous, standard-library-only, with no I/O,
local time/random, async, runtime/cache/logging effects or first-party unsafe.
No new crate is needed. Names are proposals; semantic distinctions are required.

**A-M1-01 — identity/admission.** Add distinct validated values for TenantId,
GroupId, RecoveryId, RequestId, Revision and committed command format version.
An opaque binary WorkflowId/RecordId must never be text-normalized. Group and
recovery belong to the original request scope, independently of placement
hints; ordinary restart preserves them, disaster restore changes recovery.
The domain receives an authoritative `CommandScope` and placement view, rather
than credentials or a client-provided authority boolean. Application later
authorizes current tenant scope before all submission and retained lookup.
Admission separately bounds each value, full composed/routed keys, payload and
result bytes, batch items/touched records, policy states and aggregate work.
Compatibility admission preserves reserved names, priority 0..2, required
fence even when zero, absent versus empty/null and exact numeric maxima where
the original assertions require them. Allocation/storage failures are outer
operational errors; they never become retained business rejections.

**A-M1-02 — definition/policy installation.** Introduce a typed definition
(fixed workflow type, initial state, declared logical states/modes/retry
defaults) and a full normalized policy plus `PolicyPatch` and `InstallMode`.
Use `decide_install(existing, migration_high_water, install)` returning a pure
bounded policy-write/outcome plan. Check expected generation against stored
generation before allocating; choose `max(stored,migration)+1`, checked against
the selected source generation bound. Definition install defaults replace;
low-level set defaults patch. Patch may delete a state explicitly, while
replacement removes unspecified old state configuration. Frozen default
normalization is separate from policy-dependent absence. Reject running as a
declared execution state, malformed policies and stale/conflicting generation.
Retry-only InstalledRetryPolicy stays an explicitly partial read view; it cannot
claim full policy install, generation distribution or governance parity.
M5 must extend the typed full policy for governance/retention/index fields
before their counterparts pass; unsupported fields may never be silently lost.
One initial group removes cross-group policy distribution. If multiple groups
are enabled later, the source all-shard generation fence contract still needs
an explicit distribution/availability protocol before that parity passes.

**A-M1-03 — group/partition batch.** `decide_group_batch(coherent_view,
committed_batch)` consumes a nonempty bounded ordered batch and returns a
bounded ordered write set only after every atomic member validates. Validate
tenant, group, recovery, authoritative placement, unique identity and aggregate
limits first; revalidate state/lease/fence/revision before publishing any plan.
Several logical partitions are legal only when authoritative placement proves
the same group. Use deterministic borrowed overlays for touched records when
source ordering requires sequential operations; do not clone a whole partition.
Errors produce no record/index/history/policy writes for that atomic group.
Application cross-group bulk partitions the original ordered items and returns
one result per original slot: a group error is copied to each member of that
group while independent groups can succeed. It does not claim global rollback.
Independent mode preserves per-item effects/errors and its separate dedup
identity. Parent/child resolution requires bounded same-group placement;
cross-group fanout remains explicit unsupported until a saga gate passes.

**A-M1-04 — deterministic time and encoding.** Define versioned explicit
prepared inputs (trusted commit stamp, generated IDs/tokens, retry jitter,
configuration/placement/policy generation) separately from client intent.
Neither reducer nor durable replay may obtain unstamped local inputs.
Proposed routine rule for coordinator's time ADR: an admissible stamped entry
advances group time by `max(previous, stamp)` for accepted, rejected, duplicate,
tick and membership entries; a malformed/untrusted stamp fails before proposal.
Domain deadline arithmetic is checked. Duplicate outcome preserves its original
time/result even though current processing advances control metadata. Legacy
explicit `now_ms` scenarios use a separate compatibility path, retaining source
values and ordering; they do not authorize public clients to advance trusted
group time. An idle tick policy and measured skew/forward-jump/new-leader
admission envelope remain deployment gates. Group logical time is a proposed
Rust rule, not a statement that legacy wall/HLC expirations are identical.
Use an explicit stable committed codec/version and bounded decode; do not
serialize Rust memory layout or reuse network/intent encoding as a durable
format by accident. Exact versioned committed bytes replay deterministically.

**A-M1-05 — request identity/replay.** Domain pure comparison can use a fixed
validated digest value. Application owns the version-1 typed normalization
and SHA-256 implementation described in `transports/intent-digest.md` (already
selected grammar), not the wire adapter or client. Dedup key is
tenant + original group + recovery + request ID. Prepared timestamps, generated
IDs/jitter, credentials, tracing, timeout and transport call IDs are excluded
from client-intent comparison; explicit guards, payload bytes, semantic
partition, requested schedule times and meaningful batch order are included.
`decide_request(retained, committed)` returns original accepted/rejected
outcome for matching intent before reevaluating any changed record guard.
Different intent deterministically conflicts and preserves the original
retained record. The result distinguishes original outcome position from
current applied entry position. Already-applied log replay is a separate
log-identity check and never mints new fence/history/outcome. Retention expiry,
incompatible recovery scope and authorization denial are distinct from intent
conflict. Legacy no-ID duplicate effects remain their current-history guard
path and cannot be made passing by manufacturing a shared request ID.

Required M1 exit evidence is source-derived red/green cases plus independent
model/replay coverage: malformed admission before proposal; all default/patch/
replace/CAS generation observations; two logical partitions in one group with
late guard failure and no writes/history; cross-group ordered result expansion;
independent success retention; duplicate accepted and rejected requests after
lease/revision/time changes; changed payload/guard/order/version conflict;
recovery mismatch; duplicate vs original positions; fence/time overflow;
accepted/rejected/duplicate/tick/membership nondecreasing time; deterministic
encoding vectors and source deep-FIFO lane heads. Passing these pure plans
does not establish M2 persistence, M3 consensus, M4 authorization or full parity.

## Current library candidates and adapter proof gates

Primary docs and exact published package sources were checked on 2026-10-09.
Documentation discovery reported OpenRaft 0.9.25, redb 4.3.0, rustls 0.23.45
and tokio-rustls 0.26.6. Exact crates were read in memory from
`https://static.crates.io/crates/<name>/<name>-<version>.crate`, without installing
dependencies or changing Cargo policy. Their Cargo manifests confirm redb's
edition 2024/MSRV 1.90, rustls/tokio-rustls MSRV 1.71; OpenRaft does not declare
a package rust-version, so the locked complete graph must compile on workspace
1.99.0. These are evaluation pins, not adoption/security or crash-test results.
Root alone can change manifests/policy after the ordered predecessor gate.

**A-L1 — redb 4.3.0 is the first durable adapter candidate.** Its exact
[published manifest](https://docs.rs/crate/redb/4.3.0/source/Cargo.toml) has a
small default std profile; omit experimental multiprocess/cursor/API features.
[Database](https://docs.rs/redb/4.3.0/redb/struct.Database.html) has concurrent
readers and one writer; begin_write can block. Use a bounded storage worker/
queue, never blocking fsync on an async reactor. Count jobs and bytes and keep
permits through underlying work, including a canceled response waiter.
One database per group is a reasonable initial topology; sharing a database
across groups is an explicit serialization/performance choice, not additional
atomicity. View pin lifetime is bounded and measured during snapshots/queries.

[Immediate durability](https://docs.rs/redb/4.3.0/redb/enum.Durability.html)
persists a successful commit; None cannot acknowledge a durable workflow or
Raft completion. Explicitly set/verify Immediate for authoritative, vote/log
and snapshot activation writes. The exact
[WriteTransaction](https://docs.rs/redb/4.3.0/redb/struct.WriteTransaction.html)
contract distinguishes TransactionPoisoned rollback from other commit errors,
which may already be durable and prohibit further writes until reopen. Classify
the latter as uncertain operational commit: close serving/apply, reopen, read
full checkpoint/log/outcome identity, reconcile old-or-new atomic state and
only then retry/resume. Never convert it to DomainError, publish a speculative
memory record or assume the failed call rolled back. The default one-phase
checksum commit and optional two-phase fsync mode need explicit deployment
choice and measured cost. A reader's transaction is not a complete backup.

M2 proof: one write transaction contains all records, authoritative due/FIFO/
ownership indexes, policy/fence state, events, retained outcomes/digests, group
time, membership/checkpoint as relevant. Kill a real subprocess at acknowledged
before/after commit boundaries, restart a fresh adapter from the same files,
and compare with an independent model. Inject actual backend read/write/commit
errors, truncated/corrupt bytes and capacity failure. Prove uncertain commit
reconciliation, deterministic rejection atomicity, nonwrapping fences and
matching request replay without another event. Snapshot capture uses one
coherent committed read generation, bounded streaming/manifest validation,
staged install and durable activation; crash leaves a complete old or new
generation. Prove rebuild/activation before claim service. Engine README/ACID
claims do not discharge these tests.

**A-L2 — OpenRaft 0.9.25 with explicit storage-v2.** Exact package
`src/storage/v2.rs:29-34` makes its sealed trait blanket implementation available
with storage-v2; the
[feature documentation](https://docs.rs/openraft/0.9.25/openraft/docs/feature_flags/index.html)
confirms direct separate log/state-machine traits and disables the legacy
Adapter path. Enable the reviewed feature explicitly. Keep default
multithreaded/Tokio runtime; do not accidentally enable bench, bt/nightly,
singlethreaded or compatibility features. Add Serde only for the private
selected peer/persistence codec, never to expose Raft types inward.

Implement local generic `LogBridge<P>`, `ApplyBridge<P>` and snapshot-builder
wrappers in `wf-consensus`, with OpenRaft types confined there. `wf-storage`
implements neutral `wf-ports` contracts; node wires concrete instances. No
storage-to-consensus edge, erased fake durable store or extra bridge crate is
needed by the inspected signatures. Direct traits are not dyn-compatible;
generic wrappers or object-safe neutral ports are the deliberate choices.
A compile-only temporary proof, if assigned by root, demonstrates trait
ownership only; the real backend conformance remains mandatory.

The [log trait](https://docs.rs/openraft/0.9.25/openraft/storage/trait.RaftLogStorage.html)
requires consecutive logs, serialized vote/log write I/O, durable save_vote
return and durable LogFlushed callback. append may return before its callback
but entries must already be readable. Initial bridge can await actual durable
write and then callback; it must never callback from memory/queued work. Neutral
ports carry term/leader+index identity, vote, bytes/version, range bounds,
purged metadata and operational errors losslessly. Truncate is inclusive from
the supplied log; purge is inclusive through it. Retain purged identity across
restart and never truncate applied/committed history. Ordered physical writes
and durability completions are distinct from workflow atomic transactions.

The [state-machine trait](https://docs.rs/openraft/0.9.25/openraft/storage/trait.RaftStateMachine.html)
allows either persistent state or reconstruction from a persistent snapshot.
This architecture chooses persistent state: each accepted/rejected/duplicate
entry, checkpoint and membership is durable before apply returns. Reports
from applied_state must describe persisted authority. Store one response per
applied entry in order. Build snapshots from one pinned version; install must
activate the complete validated state and current snapshot before returning.
OpenRaft's example memory store never qualifies for M2/M3 workflow success.

Use [get_read_log_id/ensure_linearizable](https://docs.rs/openraft/0.9.25/openraft/raft/struct.Raft.html)
for the selected quorum leader barrier and prove the backend has durably applied
its required identity before reading one coherent view. A numeric local
checkpoint or get_read_log_id alone is not enough. Use the library's
[learner/membership flow](https://docs.rs/openraft/0.9.25/openraft/docs/cluster_control/dynamic_membership/index.html);
authenticate the actual configured peer/node identity, not just its address.
Run [Suite::test_all](https://docs.rs/openraft/0.9.25/openraft/docs/getting_started/index.html)
against the real durable adapters, followed by three-node crash, minority,
lost-reply, restart, old-leader, snapshot and membership tests. This complete
graph/fault evidence, not a trait compile, closes M3.

Coordinator approved a finite compile-only temporary bridge probe. Actual
[source](/private/tmp/ferricstore2-architecture-bridge-1417/src/lib.rs),
[manifest](/private/tmp/ferricstore2-architecture-bridge-1417/Cargo.toml),
lockfile and stdout remain under that directory. Generic local wrappers over
an std-only refusing port implement RaftLogReader/RaftLogStorage,
RaftStateMachine and RaftSnapshotBuilder. Every effect method refuses; no
runtime/workflow/log/snapshot operation was executed. The code also compiles
lossless default LogId conversion with term:u64, leader_node:u64, index:u64.
Exact published `leader_id_adv.rs` aliases CommittedLeaderId to the complete
term/node value; single-term-leader would erase node and is unselected.

On rustc 1.99.0 b940084d7 (aarch64-apple-darwin), Cargo generate-lockfile and
locked check exited 0; formatted final locked/offline check exited 0.
The same source with bridge-v2 disabled exited 101 with E0277 inaccessible
Sealed errors for both direct wrapper implementations, an actual feature-gate
negative proof. Logs are `compile.log`, `final-check.log` and
`without-storage-v2.log`; compiler details are `compiler.txt`.
Final source SHA-256 is
`66271d9093d8ef0bc12d8c4c597e6eee2a93cc2d75dce3009d29be3d04367629`;
Cargo.lock SHA-256 is
`091b86541c1701fd9c473fb521b887c44bbfb16fad7147027f61ffe34cc73e20`.
This proves exact trait ownership, selected feature and bounds only. It does
not implement/approve operational conversion, codec, neutral durable port
signatures, real backend conformance, fsync, quorum or snapshots.

**A-L3 — rustls 0.23.45 plus tokio-rustls 0.26.6.** Exact package manifests
and [rustls docs](https://docs.rs/rustls/0.23.45/rustls/) show configurable
aws-lc-rs/ring providers. Evaluate explicit default-features=false and std plus
one provider, with matching tokio-rustls provider feature. aws-lc-rs follows the
upstream production/default choice; ring is an alternative only after target/
transitive audit or build evidence favors it. Select one provider explicitly
at node configuration; record audited transitive native/unsafe dependencies
without claiming dependency-wide unsafe freedom. Both package MSRVs fit 1.99,
but selected transitive features must still pass all platform checks.

Configure TLS1.3 explicitly even if another Cargo edge enables tls12. Preserve
HTTP ALPN h2/http/1.1 versus TCP wf-tcp/1 and separate listeners/configurations
for client, peer and admin identities. The
[ServerConfig](https://docs.rs/rustls/0.23.45/rustls/server/struct.ServerConfig.html)
has no early data at max_early_data_size=0; keep half-RTT and key logging off.
Isolate ticket/session stores and verifier policies across distinct audiences.
Per-request tenant authorization/expiry/revocation stays in shared application
admission; a TLS session does not authorize every operation indefinitely.

[tokio-rustls stream semantics](https://docs.rs/tokio-rustls/0.26.6/tokio_rustls/)
require flushing buffered writes to the socket. Bound TLS handshake, buffers,
body/frame assembly and stalled output; flush/socket completion still does not
prove the client received an outcome. Preserve retained command reconciliation
after disconnect/cancel and keep byte/output permits until actual ownership
ends. M4 proof tests wrong identities/ALPN, client cert and bearer expiry,
disabled early data, rotation/isolated resumption, fragmented/slow handshakes,
HTTP/TCP cross-replay, slow readers and bounded graceful drain with submitted
work. No TLS/parser/crypto implementation or first-party unsafe is justified.

Initial next-phase recommendation is therefore to spike redb + OpenRaft behind
the existing neutral ports, and rustls/tokio-rustls behind effect-only listeners
after M2/M3. Fail a library's concrete gate before substituting another engine;
do not use a memory implementation, relax durability or add a dependency cycle
to make a milestone look complete. No actual adapter/fault test has yet run in
this architecture review.

## Private committed codec contract before dependent implementation

**A-PC1 — root accepted after actual module/graph reads.** Put consensus-neutral
owned/borrowed prepared command values in existing `wf-ports::consensus`; keep
one private codec under existing `wf-ports::log`, with narrow typed encode/decode
functions for approved outer preparation/apply adapters. Application, storage
and consensus already depend on ports; ports depends only on types/domain.
No first-party arrow, public wire codec or storage/consensus cycle is added.
Application-only encoding would make later decoder sharing unavailable; the
alternative consensus-owned codec would require encoding behind a typed submit
port and is unnecessary for the present pure preparation contract.

Private payload bytes cover format, complete request namespace, intent version/
digest, trusted stamp and explicit represented operation/guards/generated inputs.
Exclude the separately assigned `LogIdentity` and PreparedDigest itself. Compute
SHA-256 over exact payload bytes and join it to the lossless adapter log identity
at apply. This avoids preassigning Raft positions or a self-referential digest.
Current installed retry/mode policy comes from coherent apply authority, never
a client payload. Encoder derives field-bound key/value slices; decoder enforces
count/byte/depth/checked lengths before allocating and exact typed byte binding.
Unknown format/tag, malformed optionality, duplicate map keys, truncation,
overflow and trailing bytes are operational corruption, not retained business
outcomes. Policy construction must use validated domain contracts.

Root will extend the audited exact SHA2 approval to ports through a new ADR,
manifest/policy and negative controls; ADR-005's application-only approval does
not silently authorize that edge. Domain/types/wire stay hash/effect-free.
Independent exact bytes/digest and malformed boundary controls precede M1
codec acceptance. Durable log/state/snapshot formats, atomic transactions,
uncertain commit recovery, OpenRaft suite and real fault tests still gate M2/M3.

Rust permits a single module file, and its documented modern nested layout is
parent.rs plus parent/child.rs; a directory is needed when responsibility is
split across child modules. [Rust module filenames](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/items/modules.html)
support this exact current pattern. Cargo documents tests/<target>/main.rs plus
child files for a multi-file integration target; the two grouped targets follow
that convention. [Cargo package layout](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/guide/project-layout.html)
The existing underscore target names are preserved compatibility identities;
this review proposes no rename. Module ancestry and re-exports determine public
access, while directory placement alone grants none. [Rust visibility](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/visibility-and-privacy.html)

#### Exact responsibility amendment required

| Responsibility | Required owner and limitation |
| --- | --- |
| Canonical normalized V2 semantic VALUE bytes | Pure domain closed operations inspect actual complete candidate, borrowed value or borrowed bytes and the SAME private profile/charge. Structural scan, semantic admission, measurement, copy/emission and canonical streaming correspondence belong with that owner. |
| FWCP header, request/operation dispatch, outer derived keys and prepared digest | Ports retains its private framing implementation, neutral owned boundary and SHA dependency. The V2 VALUE byte owner does not transfer the FWCP envelope to domain. |
| Existing V1 policy/claim/batch codecs, bytes and APIs | Remain ports-owned and unchanged. No automatic conversion recovers outer absent/present-empty fields that V1 erased. |
| Raw public normalization, source ETF/reference hashing, complete install and public atomic parent | Mandatory separate successors. A normalized VALUE result supplies none of their authority or compatibility by itself. |

The required future ADR006 amendment must explicitly narrow its current
single-codec statement to the private prepared FWCP codec in ports, and name
the canonical normalized V2 VALUE exception in domain. It must preserve V1
responsibility, immutable bytes/APIs/vectors and the ports-only hash edge,
and state that the private VALUE format is not the source ETF format or its
public reference hash. Its error and one-account correspondence obligations
must be explicit, with appropriate interface/path negative controls before
new artifacts are assigned. No ADR wording is edited or approved as a final
patch in this phase.

Domain continues to depend only on std and wf-types. There is no ports
backedge, SHA/serde dependency, I/O, OS, transport or execution edge. Ports
can call closed semantic domain operations through its existing dependency.
The direction requires one canonical VALUE implementation; a second ports
encoder or claimed verification flag cannot stand in for correspondence.

Rust has no cross-crate friend visibility. Merely exporting the charge type,

Exact new shared default implementation:

```rust
//! Existing default claimed fixture for the guard/retry integration suites.

use super::support::{Scenario, TestError};
use wf_domain::claim::Claim;
use wf_domain::lease::LeaseToken;
use wf_domain::workflow::{CommittedCommand, Create, Operation, reduce};
use wf_types::identity::RecordId;
use wf_types::version::TimestampMillis;

impl Scenario {
    pub(crate) fn claimed(id: &[u8], now: u64) -> Result<Self, TestError> {
        let id = RecordId::new(id.to_vec())?;
        let create = CommittedCommand {
            id: id.clone(),
            now: TimestampMillis::new(now),
            operation: Operation::Create(Create {
                workflow_type: b"fencing-type".to_vec(),
                state: b"queued".to_vec(),
                payload: Some(b"payload".to_vec()),
                run_at: Some(TimestampMillis::new(now)),
            }),
        };
        let (_, write, event) = reduce(None, &create)?.into_parts();
        let mut scenario = Self {
            record: write.ok_or("create did not emit a record")?.record,
            history: vec![event.ok_or("create did not emit history")?],
        };
        scenario.apply(
            now,
            Operation::Claim(Claim {
                expected_state: b"queued".to_vec(),
                worker: b"fencing-worker".to_vec(),
                token: LeaseToken::new(b"opaque-committed-token".to_vec())?,
                lease_ms: 30_000,
            }),
        )?;
        Ok(scenario)
    }
}
```

Exact existing generic support replacement:

```rust
//! Local deterministic single-record scenario helper; no runtime dependency.

use wf_domain::history::{EventKind, HistoryEntry};
use wf_domain::lease::LeaseGuard;
use wf_domain::workflow::{CommittedCommand, Operation, Outcome, WorkflowRecord, reduce};
use wf_types::version::TimestampMillis;

pub(crate) type TestError = Box<dyn std::error::Error>;
pub(crate) type TestResult = Result<(), TestError>;

pub(crate) struct Scenario {
    pub(crate) record: WorkflowRecord,
    pub(crate) history: Vec<HistoryEntry>,
}

impl Scenario {
    pub(crate) fn guard(&self) -> Result<LeaseGuard, TestError> {
        Ok(LeaseGuard {
            token: self
                .record
                .lease()
                .ok_or("record has no lease")?
                .token
                .clone(),
            fence: self.record.fence(),
        })
    }

    pub(crate) fn command(&self, now: u64, operation: Operation) -> CommittedCommand {
        CommittedCommand {
            id: self.record.id().clone(),
            now: TimestampMillis::new(now),
            operation,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn apply(&mut self, now: u64, operation: Operation) -> Result<Outcome, TestError> {
        let command = self.command(now, operation);
        let input = self.record.clone();
        let first = reduce(Some(&self.record), &command)?;
        assert_eq!(
            first,
            reduce(Some(&self.record), &command)?,
            "deterministic replay"
        );
        assert_eq!(self.record, input, "borrowed authoritative input mutated");
        let (outcome, write, event) = first.into_parts();
        match (write, event) {
            (Some(write), Some(event)) => {
                assert_eq!(write.expected_version, Some(self.record.version()));
                assert_eq!(write.record.version(), event.version);
                self.record = write.record;
                self.history.push(event);
            }
            (None, None) => {}
            _ => return Err("record/history write cardinality differs".into()),
        }
        Ok(outcome)
    }

    pub(crate) fn count(&self, kind: EventKind) -> usize {
        self.history
            .iter()
            .filter(|entry| entry.kind == kind)
            .count()
    }
}
```

## ARCH-NEXT-M2-STATE-CONTRACT1-MECHANICS1

The following finite choices close the proposal's grammar/accounting questions for the forthcoming named batch. They authorize no artifact creation independently of CREATE1.

Primitive format: four literal magic bytes FWSC/FWSR/FWSO, then u16 BE version1. Integers are unsigned BE of their named width; raw means u32 BE length plus exact bytes. Every optional has tag0 (absent) or1 (present); present-empty raw stays present. Unknown option/event tags, truncation and trailing bytes fail. No Rust layout, UTF-8 normalization, serde, physical ordered-key format or checksum/durability certificate is implied.

FWSC order: raw group, raw recovery, current HLC physical:u64/logical:u16/wall:u64, last-entry flag. Absent ends there. Present adds log term:u64/leader_node:u64/index:u64, prepared digest32, stamp tag0 Unstamped or1 Stamped followed by its ORIGINAL physical:u64/logical:u16/wall:u64. Current max clocks never substitute for that stamp; applied index0 remains present.

FWSR order: raw group, recovery, tenant, partition; priority:u8; state_enter_seq:u128; raw id, workflow_type, state; version:u64, fence:u64, attempts:u64, created_at:u64, updated_at:u64; optional next_run_at:u64; optional raw run_state; optional lease containing raw worker, raw token, deadline:u64; optional raw payload, result, error; latest kind:u8, latest_version:u64, latest_fence:u64. Event tags in order0..12 are Created,Claimed,Transitioned,Completed,Failed,Retry,LeaseExtended,Cancelled,ChildCompleted,ChildFailed,ChildCancelled,ChildrenCancelled,ChildrenSpawned. Ordering priority is0..2; sequence is exact u128. All existing restoration consistency rules, including the selected generated-due fix, apply.

FWSO order: raw tenant, group, recovery, request; intent version:u16,digest32; original log term:u64/leader_node:u64/index:u64; original_time:u64,expires_at:u64; response_version:u16; raw response. Do not redundantly serialize typed RetainedStatus. The ONE new pure server-only API is record_batch_retained_status(intent:ClientIntent,response_version:u16,response:&[u8])->Result<RetainedStatus,CodecError>, implemented without allocation in the EXISTING ports record_batch response module, parent wrapper and log reexport. It owns intent5/response1 gating and the existing closed response-table authority. Storage decode derives status there; storage encode compares that returned status to the supplied owner. No rejection table copy in storage, alternate helper name or second response API is selected.

Every codec takes an explicit positive maximum_bytes; no global default/profile model is added. Encode validates actual immutable values and measures before one fallible output reservation. Record admission reuses existing record_bytes through a narrow public visibility/doc seam with unchanged body. Decode checks cap, header and complete structural framing/EOF before allocating output owners, then namespace/typed-value consistency; all length arithmetic is checked. Conservative family bounds for tests are FWSC<=1024, FWSR<=checked(B+131072), FWSO<=16384 where B is decision_bytes. begin_apply borrows group/recovery for its store-borrow lifetime and uses the accurately named maximum_read_steps plus maximum_read_bytes. due_cursor uses &'tx self, &'tx TenantId, ClaimQuery<'tx> and Option<DueOrder<'tx>> so filters/continuation need no hidden copies. One step is consumed before each control, point, membership, head or cursor-open attempt, including misses; range traversal additionally counts EVERY physically inspected candidate before filtering and any empty range-end probe. Repeated latched terminal returns do no new backend work. The cursor's maximum_rows is its returned-row cap, separate from cumulative steps; local positive byte/row caps are constrained by remaining transaction limits.

Logical read bytes are cumulative, without refund or page reset: control512; each copied/returned StoredWorkflowRecord or RetainedOutcome is512 plus ALL its owned variable bytes (including tenant/partition or all scope/request/response owners); each inspected semantic due key is128 plus its id/partition/state/type bytes. A record materialized to filter a candidate incurs its record charge even when discarded. Boolean/miss/empty results have no copied output-byte charge but consume their step. Borrowed query/input donors, backend pages/cache/read versions/queued jobs and caller copies are outside this logical profile; no all-live or native bound is claimed. Admission precedes output ownership/visible cursor progress. Point refusal is Limit; cursor exhaustion is BudgetEnd preserving the last emitted resume position. RangeEnd alone certifies the actual requested range was exhausted under the same transaction.

GroupApplyChanges owns the plan, borrows the request scope and stores expected ControlState. Construction checks the plan's coherent next-control relation and Fresh/Replay outcome namespace; commit must compare exact expected predecessor/control, group/recovery and affected record versions against the same transaction, preserving global group control across tenants. This sealed mathematical container is not proof of origin/durability. KnownAborted is unchanged durable predecessor; Uncertain requires fencing and durable reconciliation. No backend, driver, new budget model or general KV layer is added by these choices.
